problem: Embodied navigation agents in realistic 3D scans were deaf: simulators such as Habitat rendered only RGB, depth and semantics, with no acoustically correct audio. Earlier audio-based agent studies used non-photorealistic game boards, used no physically correct sound models, and trained and tested in the same environment. No end-to-end agent had been shown to navigate unmapped, realistic environments using sound.
motivation: Sound tells an agent where a target is even when it is out of view or occluded (a ringing phone behind a sofa, someone calling from another room). Reverberation also exposes room geometry, doors, obstacles and materials, which complements vision. The paper's driving observation is that the acoustic pressure field decays along the geodesic path, not the Euclidean one. Audio can therefore guide an agent through doorways as intermediate goals, whereas a GPS displacement vector points straight through walls.
key_idea: The paper builds SoundSpaces, which precomputes geometric-acoustics room impulse responses for every source-listener pair on dense grids in Replica and Matterport3D inside Habitat. On top of it, a PPO agent is trained end-to-end on binaural spectrograms plus RGB/depth to navigate to a sounding target (AudioGoal) or to an audio-plus-point goal (AudioPointGoal).
insight: Audio carries both goal-direction cues and geometric cues, so it adds information beyond a perfect GPS pointer. AudioPointGoal beats PointGoal for every visual sensor, e.g., Replica Blind 0.480→0.681 SPL and MP3D Depth 0.541→0.581. AudioGoal with depth and no GPS matches or beats PointGoal with perfect GPS (0.756 vs 0.601 on Replica; 0.552 vs 0.541 on MP3D). AudioGoal is immune to GPS noise, and AudioPointGoal degrades more gracefully than PointGoal as GPS noise grows. The intensity-only ablation shows the agent exploits more than a loudness gradient: using only left/right RMS drops AudioGoal-Depth SPL from 0.756 to 0.291 (Replica) and from 0.552 to 0.014 (MP3D). Supporting evidence: t-SNE shows the learned audio features encode goal distance and direction, and 40 dB SNR microphone noise barely hurts (0.756→0.753; 0.552→0.550). The weakness is generalization to new sounds: AudioGoal falls to 0.454 / 0.338 SPL on unheard sounds, while AudioPointGoal stays robust (0.707 / 0.538) because it can rebalance toward the displacement vector.
method: SoundSpaces acoustic simulation: bidirectional path tracing with multiple importance sampling adapted for room acoustics, run in 4 log-spaced frequency bands up to 200 bounces. Semantic mesh labels are mapped to acoustic materials (absorption, scattering, transmission coefficients), which allows sound transmission through walls. Early reflections are clustered separately. Output is 2nd-order ambisonic RIRs, converted to binaural.

Dense RIR grid: source and listener points on a 0.5 m (Replica, 18 scenes) or 1 m (Matterport3D, 85 scenes) grid at 1.5 m height, pruned by a ray-traced closed-ness test (C_min 0.5, d_min 5 cm). RIRs are precomputed for all N^2 pairs; audio for any source-listener pair is rendered on the fly by convolving an arbitrary waveform with the stored RIR.

Navigability graph and tasks: an edge joins neighboring grid nodes if their geodesic and Euclidean distances are equal. AudioGoal gives audio only (no GPS); AudioPointGoal gives audio plus an idealized displacement vector; PointGoal gives the displacement vector only. Success requires Stop exactly at the goal node within 500 actions; there is no actuation noise, and the goal is invisible.
Audio encoding: binaural STFT (hop 160, window 512) over the first 1 s, log magnitude downsampled 4x, giving 65x65x2 (Replica, 44.1 kHz) or 65x26x2 (MP3D, 16 kHz) tensors.

Policy network: two separately weighted CNNs (conv 8x8, 4x4, 3x3 + linear, 512-d each) encode audio and the RGB or depth image (128x128, 90° FoV). Their outputs are concatenated with the displacement vector Δ (when available) and fed to a GRU (hidden size 512); linear actor and critic heads sit on top.

Training: PPO with reward +10 for Stop at goal, −0.01 per step, and ±1 for decreasing/increasing geodesic distance, plus an entropy bonus. Adam with lr 2.5e-4, γ = 0.99. Runs are 30M steps on Replica (105 GPU-h) and 60M steps on MP3D (210 GPU-h).

setting.backbone: separate 3-layer CNN encoders for audio spectrogram and RGB/depth + GRU actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces episodes rendered in Habitat: 0.1M training episodes on Replica and 2M on Matterport3D, in scenes disjoint from test. Default sound source is a telephone ring; the varied-sound experiments draw on 102 freesound.org clips split 73/11/18 (train/val/test). No external data or pretraining.
setting.observation: egocentric binaural audio (spectrogram) + monocular RGB or depth (128x128, 90° FoV), or blind; idealized GPS displacement vector for AudioPointGoal/PointGoal only
setting.action_space: discrete grid-graph moves: MoveForward 0.5 m (Replica) / 1 m (Matterport3D), TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop; 500-action horizon; no actuation noise
setting.simulator: Habitat + SoundSpaces precomputed RIRs (Replica and Matterport3D)
setting.privileged: AudioGoal: none. AudioPointGoal/PointGoal: perfect GPS displacement to goal. All tasks: agent constrained to precomputed grid nodes with noiseless actuation.

numbers_note: The paper reports only SPL, printed as fractions (e.g. 0.756, entered here as 75.6). SR, NE and similar metrics are not reported. The Replica and Matterport3D parts of SoundSpaces are listed separately under bench 'SoundSpaces', with the dataset named in the method and extra fields; both use unseen test scenes (1000 test episodes each). Blind and RGB variants, and the vision-only PointGoal agent the authors trained, appear in Tables 2 and 3 but are omitted here to respect the variant limit. The GPS-noise curve (Fig. 5a) is given only as a figure. The supplement is inconsistent about the sound split: it says '73/11/18 splits' but also 'we train using the 78 sounds'. The later-standard heard/unheard AudioGoal protocol with SR/SPL/SNA comes from follow-up work, not this paper.
results: Audio improves navigation across all visual sensors. AudioPointGoal beats a vision-plus-GPS PointGoal PPO agent, e.g., 0.709 vs 0.601 SPL (Replica, depth) and 0.581 vs 0.541 (MP3D, depth); every learned agent far outperforms the non-learning baselines (Random, Forward, Goal Follower ≤ 0.197). AudioGoal, which has no GPS at all, reaches 0.756 SPL on Replica and 0.552 on MP3D, exceeding PointGoal with perfect GPS. Performance is robust to microphone noise but drops sharply for AudioGoal on unheard sounds (0.454 / 0.338).
limitations: Discretized, grid-constrained navigation: the agent can only occupy precomputed RIR nodes (0.5 m / 1 m), turns are discrete, actuation is noiseless, and success requires stopping exactly on the goal node. This is far from continuous or real-robot settings.
A single static sound source, repeatedly emitting, with an invisible goal. Generalization to unheard sounds is poor for AudioGoal (Replica depth 0.756→0.454 SPL).
Only SPL is reported, and there is no sim-to-real validation; the geometric-acoustics simulation needs special handling for low-frequency wave effects such as diffraction.
